CatalogAccessFilterUpsert.description:
Full-replace upsert body for one ``(sub, component_type)`` filter row.

The path names the subject and this body names the
``component_type``. The two together are the primary key, so modules
and inverters carry independent access rules per user.

``component_ids`` defaults to an empty list. With ``mode=allow``
that is a deliberate lockout and the caller sees nothing. With
``mode=deny`` it is the unrestricted default. Both shapes are valid and
the controller accepts them without warning.

The two ``download_files_*_list`` fields gate the download channel only
(ignored on list / JSON wire) keyed on version UUID. Empty
``download_files_allow_list`` = no allow-list restriction. Non-empty =
download restricted to listed UUIDs only. ``download_files_deny_list``
is evaluated after the allow check and blocks even otherwise-allowed
files. See :meth:`CatalogAccessFilter.file_allowed_for_download`.

component_type.description: 'module' or 'inverter'. Names the catalog table this filter targets.

download_files_allow_list.description: Download channel only: explicit allow-list of version UUIDs. Empty = no allow-list restriction. Non-empty = downloads restricted to listed UUIDs.
download_files_allow_list.title: Download Files Allow List

download_files_deny_list.description: Download channel only: explicit deny-list of version UUIDs. Evaluated AFTER the allow-list. Listed UUIDs are blocked from download even if otherwise visible.
download_files_deny_list.title: Download Files Deny List

mode.description: 'allow' restricts to ``component_ids``. 'deny' restricts to everything but ``component_ids``.
mode.title: Mode

DeleteCountResponse.description:
Unified DELETE response shape.

Every DELETE on the admin controllers returns ``deleted_count``
rather than ``deleted: bool`` plus 404. That covers quota defaults, overrides,
catalog access filters, field visibility overrides, and user claims.
A "miss" is ``{"deleted_count": 0}``. A caller that asserts "I deleted
exactly one" checks ``count == 1``. This collapses the prior two response shapes
(single-row ``{"deleted": True}`` and bulk ``{"deleted_count": N}``)
so the admin UI can use one decoder for every DELETE.
DeleteCountResponse.title: DeleteCountResponse

Upsert body for one override row. The subject is the path segment.

The override is split per channel. The list pair
(``add_fields_list`` / ``remove_fields_list``) controls JSON wire
visibility, and the download pair (``add_fields_download`` /

removed. To narrow the download set, populate

info.description:
The **Renewables Component Library** is a curated catalog of approved
photovoltaic (PV) component data. It holds PAN files for solar modules and
OND files for inverters. PV simulation and yield-modelling tools read these
files as inputs.

## Authentication

All endpoints require a valid bearer token issued by Veracity OIDC. The token
is read from the `access_token` cookie (set by the SPA after `/auth/login`)
or the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

> **Want to use _Try it out_ on this page?**
>   **[-> Sign in with Veracity](/auth/login?return_url=/docs)**
>
> The docs themselves are public, but a request against a live
> endpoint needs a valid auth cookie. Click the link above and complete
> the OIDC flow. You come back here with the cookie set, and every
> _Try it out_ button on this page then works.

### Using _Try it out_

- **Read endpoints (`GET`):** sign in, click _Try it out_, then _Execute_.
- **Write endpoints (`POST` / `PUT` / `DELETE`):** sign in first, then:
  1. Call `GET /auth/csrf` and copy `csrf_token` from the response body.
  2. On the mutating endpoint, paste that value into the `X-CSRF-Token` header field.
  3. Click _Execute_. Without the header you get `403 CSRF token missing`.
- The `access_token` cookie is `HttpOnly`, so it does not appear in `document.cookie`. Confirm it is attached in the browser Network panel.

## Field projection

List and detail endpoints accept an `outputParameter` query parameter, a
comma-separated list of field names. Omitting it returns the **full spec**.
Field names are accepted in either `camelCase` or `snake_case`.

Four fields are always included regardless of projection:
`manufacturer`, `model`, `fileUuid`, `componentId`.

`fileUuid` identifies a single uploaded revision. `componentId` identifies
the logical product across all its revisions (and supersessions). Use
`componentId` to grant access via `/admin/catalog-access`.

```
# Compact list view (just identifiers)
GET /catalog/modules?outputParameter=manufacturer,model

# IV-curve parameters (electrical characterization)
GET /catalog/modules?outputParameter=pNom,isc,voc,imp,vmp

# Temperature coefficients (used for derating in simulation)
GET /catalog/modules?outputParameter=muIsc,muVocSpec,muPmpReq

# Cell layout + bifaciality
GET /catalog/modules?outputParameter=nCelS,nCelP,technol,bifacialityFactor

# Inverter efficiency curve + voltage window
GET /catalog/inverters?outputParameter=efficMax,efficEuro,vMppMin,vMppMax,vAbsMax
```

## Filtering

List endpoints accept arbitrary `filter.<field>[.<op>]=<value>` query
parameters. Multiple filters are combined with **AND**.

| Operator | Applies to | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `eq` (default) | any field | `filter.manufacturer=Acme` |
| `contains` | string fields | `filter.model.contains=450W` |
| `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte` | numeric fields | `filter.pNom.gte=400` |

```
# Exact match (URL-encode spaces)
GET /catalog/modules?filter.manufacturer=Acme%20Solar

# Substring match on model name
GET /catalog/modules?filter.model.contains=450

# Power rating between 400 W and 600 W
GET /catalog/modules?filter.pNom.gte=400&filter.pNom.lte=600

# Monocrystalline modules above 500 W from a specific manufacturer
GET /catalog/modules?filter.manufacturer=Acme&filter.technol=mtSiMono&filter.pNom.gte=500

# Only the records the catalog currently publishes
GET /catalog/modules?filter.lifecycleStatus=published

# Transformerless inverters with at least 4 MPPTs
GET /catalog/inverters?filter.transfo=Without&filter.nbMppt.gte=4
```

## Combining filters and projection

Filters and `outputParameter` can be mixed freely:

```
# 500 W+ modules, return only IV-curve fields
GET /catalog/modules?filter.pNom.gte=500&outputParameter=pNom,isc,voc,imp,vmp
```

## Pagination and ordering

Use `take` (default 25, max 10000) with `skip` for pagination, and `orderBy`
with `orderDir` (`ASC`/`DESC`) for sorting. The total result count is returned
alongside the items page.

```
# Page 3 of 25-item pages, sorted by power rating descending
GET /catalog/modules?take=25&skip=50&orderBy=pNom&orderDir=DESC
```

get.description: Minimal liveness payload at the sub-app root.

Returns one page of the per-`(sub, component_type)` catalog access filter rows. The optional `sub` query parameter narrows the result to one subject.

The page holds the rows under `items`, beside the `skip` and `take` it applied and the `total` the `sub` filter selects before paging. `skip + len(items) < total` means more pages remain.

Each row carries `mode` (`allow` or `deny`) and a set of `component_ids`. Together they define the effective row-level access for that caller against the published catalog. Each row also carries the two download-channel gates `download_files_allow_list` / `download_files_deny_list`, keyed on version UUID.

Subjects with no filter row for a given `component_type` see the unrestricted published catalog of that kind (the default). Admins always bypass these filters for review purposes. Requires the `admin:read` scope.

delete.description:
Removes the filter row identified by the subject in the path and the `component_type` query parameter (the composite primary key). After deletion the caller falls back to the default unrestricted view of the published catalog for that `component_type`.

Returns `{"deleted_count": N}` (0 on a miss, 1 on success) rather than 404. This matches the unified delete response shape used across every admin controller. A caller asserting 'I deleted exactly one' checks `deleted_count == 1`. The `CatalogAccessChanged` audit event fires only on a non-zero count, which keeps the audit record aligned with the state changes.

Requires the `admin:update` scope and a valid CSRF token.

put.description:
Creates or replaces the filter row for the subject in the path and the `component_type` in the body. The two are the composite primary key. Idempotent: a second write of the same pair overwrites the prior `mode`, `component_ids`, `download_files_allow_list`, and `download_files_deny_list` cleanly.

Filter semantics: `mode=allow` restricts the caller to components whose id is IN `component_ids`. `mode=deny` restricts the caller to components whose id is NOT IN `component_ids`. Every `component_ids` UUID must reference an existing identity row. Unknown ids yield 422.

An empty `component_ids` with `mode=allow` hides every component. An empty `component_ids` with `mode=deny` forbids nothing. The two `download_files_*_list` fields gate the file download only and are keyed on version UUID, not component UUID. Requires the `admin:update` scope and a valid CSRF token.

The filter row MUST already exist. Callers first create the row via `PUT /admin/catalog-access/{sub}` and then use this endpoint for incremental edits. A missing filter row yields 404. The submitted `component_id` must reference an existing identity row. Unknown ids yield 422.

The file-level allow/deny lists on the row are preserved unchanged by this endpoint. Requires the `admin:update` scope and a valid CSRF token.

get.description:
Returns one page of per-`(sub, component_type)` field visibility override rows. The optional `sub` query parameter narrows the result to one subject.

Paging uses `skip` and `take`: `skip` is the number of rows to pass over (default `0`), and `take` is the number of rows in the page (default `100`, maximum `1000`). A value outside those bounds is refused with 422 rather than clamped.

The response carries `items`, `total`, `skip` and `take`. `total` counts the rows the `sub` filter keeps before the page is cut, so `skip + items.length < total` means more pages remain. A subject holding an override on both component types counts as two rows.

Each row carries four per-surface sets that layer over the preset-default allowlist. They apply to one caller and one component kind (`module` or `inverter`). The list surface uses `add_fields_list` / `remove_fields_list` (catalog JSON wire). The download surface uses `add_fields_download` / `remove_fields_download` (file download walker).

Subjects with no override row inherit the preset default at request time. Requires the `admin:read` scope.

A caller asserting 'I deleted exactly one' checks `deleted_count == 1`. put.description:
Creates or updates one override row. The subject in the path and the `component_type` in the body are the composite key, and the body carries no subject. Idempotent: a repeated request on the same pair overwrites the prior per-channel `add_fields_*` / `remove_fields_*` sets cleanly.

The API resolves the effective allowlist per channel, with the same set algebra on both sides: `effective_list = (base | add_fields_list) - remove_fields_list` and `effective_download = (base | add_fields_download) - remove_fields_download`. The two channels differ only in the columns they populate.

Each axis follows preserve-on-omit semantics: omitting a field keeps its current stored value, sending `[]` clears it, and sending a populated list replaces it. Field names must reference real columns on the target spec table or entries of the base catalog allowlist. Unknown names yield 422. To narrow the download set, populate `remove_fields_download`. Requires the `admin:update` scope and a valid CSRF token.

Clearing every axis removes the override. The response then reports four empty sets, which is the effective state, and the subject stops appearing in `GET /admin/field-visibility-overrides`.

After the delete, the endpoint falls back to the in-code default limit for that window. Returns `{"deleted_count": N}` (0 on a miss, 1 on success) rather than 404. The unified DELETE response shape lets the admin UI make an idempotent delete without a check for existence. Requires `admin:update` plus CSRF.

Return one page of the endpoint default quotas, sorted by `(endpoint_key, window_seconds)`. A quota default row keyed on `(endpoint_key, window_seconds)` defines the baseline `limit_value` applied to every caller for that logical endpoint and window. The only `endpoint_key` that carries a quota today is `download:file`.

Page with `skip` and `take`. The response carries `items`, `total`, `skip` and `take`, where `total` counts every stored quota default before the page is cut, so `skip + len(items) < total` means another page remains. Requires `admin:read`.

put.description:
Idempotent upsert on the composite key `(endpoint_key, window_seconds)`. A replay with identical input is safe. `limit_value` and `description` are overwritten, and `updated_by` is stamped with the caller's `sub`. The new value takes effect on the next request to that endpoint. The quota default lookup runs on each request, so no cache invalidation is needed.

Use this endpoint to widen or to tighten the default for `download:file`. A per-subject exception belongs on the `/overrides` resource instead. Requires `admin:update` plus CSRF.

Return one page of the active per-`(sub, endpoint_key, window_seconds)` overrides. An override replaces the `limit_value` of the matching quota default for one subject. If no override exists, the quota default applies.

An expired row (past `expires_at`) is excluded from the listing but kept in the table for audit. Both filters (`sub`, `endpoint_key`) are optional and AND-combined. `endpoint_key` accepts `download:file`.

Page with `skip` and `take`. The response carries `items`, `total`, `skip` and `take`, where `total` counts the overrides the filters match before the page is cut, so `skip + len(items) < total` means another page remains. Requires `admin:read`.

delete.description:
One endpoint serves both single-row and bulk override deletion. The subject is the path segment. Optional query parameters: `endpoint_key` (`download:file`), `window_seconds`.

When both are supplied the route addresses exactly one row (the single-row case). When either is omitted, the missing columns are wildcarded and every matching row for the subject is removed. A request with no query resets that person to the defaults, which is the offboarding case.

Always returns `{"deleted_count": N}` (0 on a miss) rather than 404 so the admin UI can issue idempotent 'reset to defaults' actions without a check for existence. Requires `admin:update` plus CSRF.

put.description:
The subject is the path segment. The body carries `endpoint_key`, `window_seconds` and `limit_value`, plus the optional `reason` and `expires_at`. Idempotent upsert on `(sub, endpoint_key, window_seconds)`. An override takes precedence over the matching quota default and does not modify it, so a delete of the override restores the default.

A replay of one of those keys is safe. `reason` is free-form audit text. The quota store honors `expires_at` at evaluation time, so an expired override is inert but retained for audit. Requires `admin:update` plus CSRF.

get.description:
Return one page of the live counters, each joined to the effective `limit_value` for that `(sub, endpoint_key, window_seconds)` tuple. The override value applies if one exists, otherwise the quota default applies.

Rows reflect the *current* sliding window only. A counter whose window has elapsed is not returned. The same numbers drive the `X-RateLimit-*` response headers on enforced routes, and they are exposed here for admin observability. Those header names follow the IETF `RateLimit-*` convention, so they keep the `RateLimit` spelling. Both filters are optional and AND-combined. `endpoint_key` accepts `download:file`.

Page with `skip` and `take`. The response carries `items`, `total`, `skip` and `take`, where `total` counts the live counters the filters match before the page is cut, so `skip + len(items) < total` means another page remains. Requires `admin:read`.

get.description: Handles the Veracity OIDC redirect after the user authenticates. Validates the `oauth_csrf` binding cookie against the `csrf` field embedded in `state`, then exchanges the authorization `code` for ID and refresh tokens using the PKCE verifier. On success, installs the `access_token` and `refresh_token` cookies (HttpOnly, scoped to the configured cookie path) and redirects to the `return_url` carried in `state`, falling back to `/`. Anonymous-OK by design. This endpoint is what *creates* the session. Returns 400 when `code` or `state` is missing, or when the IdP redirects back with an `error` parameter.
get.summary: OIDC redirect target. Exchange code for tokens

get.description: Generates a fresh CSRF token, returns it in the JSON body as `csrf_token`, and sets the signed companion cookie. Mutating endpoints validate the pair by reading the token from the `X-CSRF-Token` request header (or `X-CSRFToken`) and comparing the signature against the cookie. SPA clients should call this once after login (or whenever a 403 indicates a stale token) and cache the value in memory for subsequent POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE calls. Anonymous-OK.
get.summary: Issue a CSRF token for mutating requests

get.description: Redirects the browser to the Veracity (Azure B2C) authorize endpoint to start the OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE. The optional `return_url` query parameter is encoded into the OAuth `state` so the callback can bounce the user back to the originating SPA route after authentication. Anonymous-OK: this endpoint is the entry point and never reads existing auth cookies. Plants the short-lived `oauth_csrf` binding cookie on the redirect response so `/auth/callback` can prove the same browser completed both legs. Responds with HTTP 307 to the IdP authorize URL.

Clears the local `access_token` and `refresh_token` cookies and redirects (HTTP 303) through the Veracity end-session endpoint so the IdP terminates its SSO session too. Otherwise the next `/auth/login` would silently re-authenticate. Reads the current `access_token` cookie before deletion to pass it as `id_token_hint`, which lets Azure B2C identify the session without prompting. After IdP teardown the browser is bounced to `post_logout_redirect_uri` (or the SPA root if unset). Anonymous-OK: callable even without an active session.
get.summary: Clear local cookies and trigger RP-initiated logout

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's full profile (subject, email, name, display name) plus the effective scope set and the derived preset label. `preset` is the name of the largest named permission level whose scope set is a subset of the user's effective scopes. It is `null` when no preset matches exactly.

Effective scopes are resolved exactly as request authorization resolves them, so the response is a faithful preview of what the caller can do. Requires a valid session. Anonymous callers get 401.
get.summary: Authenticated user profile and effective scopes

post.description: Exchanges the `refresh_token` cookie for a fresh ID token (and, when the IdP policy rotates them, a new refresh token). SPA clients should call this proactively before the access token expires. The server-side silent-refresh path covers callers that do not. Reinstalls both auth cookies on the response and returns `{"ok": true}` on success. Returns 401 when the `refresh_token` cookie is absent. CSRF-exempt because it authenticates via cookie possession rather than the user-scoped session.

get.description: Returns the catalog of all scope strings and named presets supported by the API, so a client can render permission choices without hardcoding scope identifiers. Anonymous-OK: the catalog itself contains no per-user information.

Returns a privacy-minimal view of the authenticated caller: subject, display name, authentication flag, and the caller's *effective* scopes. Effective scopes come from the DB claims when the user is provisioned, and from the JWT-derived allowlisted scopes otherwise. Deliberately omits the email, the given name and the family name. Consumers that need the richer SPA profile must call `/auth/me` instead. Requires a valid session. Anonymous callers get 401.

List published OND inverter records with filtering and field projection.

    Returns the one version of each inverter component that the catalog
    serves. Filtering, projection, pagination, and authentication are
    identical to `GET /catalog/modules`. The only difference is the field
    vocabulary.

    **Required scope:** `components:list`

    ## Filterable fields

    Filters follow the same `filter.<field>[.<op>]=<value>` shape as
    `/catalog/modules`. Empty values are treated as no-ops, so the Swagger
    UI `(no filter)` dropdown is safe to leave selected.

    | Category | Fields |
    | --- | --- |
    | Identification | `manufacturer`, `model` |
    | Lifecycle | `lifecycleStatus`, `lifecycleStatusDate` |
    | AC output (numeric, **kW**) | `pNomConv`, `pMaxOut` |
    | Efficiency (numeric, **percent 0-100**) | `efficMax`, `efficEuro` |
    | DC input (numeric, V) | `vMppMin`, `vMppMax`, `vAbsMax`, `nbMppt` |
    | Topology | `transfo` |

    ### Examples

    ```
    # Inverters with at least 4 MPPTs
    GET /catalog/inverters?filter.nbMppt.gte=4

    # 80 kW to 200 kW string inverters above 98% peak efficiency
    GET /catalog/inverters?filter.pNomConv.gte=80&filter.pNomConv.lte=200&filter.efficMax.gte=98

    # Inverters within a 1500 V DC bus window
    GET /catalog/inverters?filter.vAbsMax.lte=1500
    ```

    ## Field projection examples

    ```
    # Efficiency curve + voltage window
    GET /catalog/inverters?outputParameter=pNomConv,efficMax,efficEuro,vMppMin,vMppMax

    # Power + transformer topology
    GET /catalog/inverters?outputParameter=pNomConv,pMaxOut,transfo
    ```

    ## Pagination and ordering

    Same parameters as `/catalog/modules` (`take`, `skip`, `orderBy`,
    `orderDir`). Sortable fields: `manufacturer`, `model`, `pNomConv`,
    `efficMax`, `width`, `height`, `depth`, `weight`, `lifecycleStatus`,
    `lifecycleStatusDate`. Any other field is a 400.

    ## Response shape

    ```json
    {
      "items": [
        { "manufacturer": "...", "model": "...", "fileUuid": "...", "...": "..." }
      ],
      "total": 312,
      "skip": 0,
      "take": 25
    }
    ```

    ## Restricted fields

    Same policy as `/catalog/modules`: `datasourceDate` and `validationResult`
    are not projected into the list response, and `dataSource` is projected for
    every caller.

get.description:
List published PAN module records with filtering and field projection.

    Returns the one version of each component that the catalog serves: the
    published version, or the highest numbered deprecated one when the
    component publishes none. That is the record a simulation tool should
    consume. An older version is not visible here. The version-list
    endpoints show every version, and they are admin-only.

    **Required scope:** `components:list`

    ## Filtering

    Pass any number of `filter.<field>[.<op>]=<value>` query parameters.
    Multiple filters are combined with **AND**. An empty value (e.g.
    `filter.manufacturer=`) is treated as **no filter** on that field, so
    the Swagger UI `(no filter)` dropdown options are safe to leave selected.

    | Operator | Applies to | Example |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `eq` *(default)* | any field | `filter.manufacturer=JinkoSolar` |
    | `contains` | string fields | `filter.model.contains=550` |
    | `gt` / `gte` / `lt` / `lte` | numeric fields | `filter.pNom.gte=500` |

    ### Filterable fields

    | Category | Fields |
    | --- | --- |
    | Identification | `manufacturer`, `model` |
    | Lifecycle | `lifecycleStatus`, `lifecycleStatusDate` |
    | Electrical (numeric, W) | `pNom`, `isc`, `voc`, `imp`, `vmp`, `muPmpReq`, `bifacialityFactor` |
    | Technology | `technol` (PVsyst code: `mtSiMono`, `mtSiPoly`, `mtHIT`, `mtCdTe`, `mtuCSi_aSiH`) |

    A version holds one of `draft`, `under_review`, `validated`,
    `published`, `deprecated` or `archived`. This endpoint serves only the
    two the catalog shows, so `lifecycleStatus` reads `published` or
    `deprecated` here.

    ### Examples

    ```
    # Substring search on model name
    GET /catalog/modules?filter.model.contains=550

    # Bifacial mono-Si modules between 500 W and 600 W from one manufacturer
    GET /catalog/modules?filter.manufacturer=JinkoSolar&filter.bifacialityFactor.gte=0.5&filter.pNom.gte=500&filter.pNom.lte=600

    # All monocrystalline silicon modules
    GET /catalog/modules?filter.technol=mtSiMono
    ```

    ## Field projection

    The `outputParameter` query parameter trims the returned fields. Three
    fields are **always** present on every item: `manufacturer`, `model`,
    and `fileUuid`. Omitting `outputParameter` returns the full spec
    (every non-null field the caller is allowed to see).

    Field names accept either `camelCase` or `snake_case`.

    ### Examples

    ```
    # Just power rating + identifiers
    GET /catalog/modules?outputParameter=pNom

    # IV-curve electrical parameters only
    GET /catalog/modules?outputParameter=pNom,isc,voc,imp,vmp

    # Combined: heavy modules, return only IV curve fields
    GET /catalog/modules?filter.pNom.gte=500&outputParameter=pNom,isc,voc,imp,vmp
    ```

    ## Pagination and ordering

    | Parameter | Default | Notes |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `take` | `25` | Items per page (max 10000). Use `take=0` for a count-only query. |
    | `skip` | `0` | Offset for paging. |
    | `orderBy` | `manufacturer` | Sortable: `manufacturer`, `model`, `pNom`, `technol`, `width`, `height`, `depth`, `weight`, `lifecycleStatus`, `lifecycleStatusDate`. Any other field is a 400. |
    | `orderDir` | `ASC` | Or `DESC`. Any other value is a 400. |

    The `total` field in the response is the unpaginated count. Use it to
    decide whether more pages remain: `skip + items.length < total`.

    ## Response shape

    ```json
    {
      "items": [
        { "manufacturer": "...", "model": "...", "fileUuid": "...", "...": "..." }
      ],
      "total": 1245,
      "skip": 0,
      "take": 25
    }
    ```

    Field membership inside each `items[]` entry depends on
    `outputParameter` and the caller's claims. `dataSource` is projected for
    every caller.

get.description:
Download the stored PAN or OND file for one version.

    Returns the content of the source `.PAN` (module) or `.OND` (inverter)
    file, narrowed to the fields the caller may see. Send the bytes directly
    to PVsyst or to another simulation tool that expects the native format.
    The component's type decides which of the two file kinds is served.

    **Required scope:** `components:read`

    ## Response headers

    | Header | Value |
    | --- | --- |
    | `Content-Type` | `application/octet-stream` |
    | `Content-Disposition` | `attachment; filename*=UTF-8''<rfc-5987-encoded>` |

    The `filename*=` form (RFC 5987) preserves non-ASCII characters in
    the original upload filename.

    ## Errors

    | Status | Cause |
    | --- | --- |
    | 401 | No authentication. |
    | 404 | No version with this `fileUuid`, or the catalog does not serve it to you. |
    | 422 | `file_uuid` is not a valid UUID. |

    A caller who holds no content-elevation scope reaches a version the
    catalog serves, which is a `published` or a `deprecated` one. Every
    other version answers 404 to that caller, and 404 rather than 403 so
    the response does not confirm which version ids exist.

put.description:
Move one version to the lifecycle status named in the query.

    Three targets reach this endpoint, and each is a separate reviewer act:

    | Target | Act | Moves from |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `under_review` | Submit the version for review | `draft` |
    | `validated` | Accept the technical content | `under_review` |
    | `published` | Serve the version to every caller | `validated` |

    Publishing a replacement also moves the outgoing published version to
    `deprecated`, in the same transaction, because a component holds at
    most one published version. So `deprecated` is never a target here, and
    `archived` belongs to ``POST /catalog/{fileUuid}/revoke``. Either one
    is a 400.

    The reason, and any datasheet reference or accepted deviation the
    reviewer cites, land on the version's change record, so the record
    holds the reason and not only the reviewer. A transition the lifecycle
    does not permit is a 409.

get.description:
List the change record of this version.

    **Admin only**. Requires ``components:create`` or
    ``components:update``.

    The record is append-only and newest first. Each entry names who acted,

    status it moved to. An entry that describes something else leaves both

Withdraw a served version, moving it to ``archived``.

    Requires the more privileged ``approve:revoke`` scope. Only a
    ``published`` or ``deprecated`` version may be withdrawn, and any other
    status is a 409.

    ``archived`` is terminal, so the withdrawal stays visible in the change
    record rather than being erased. Withdrawing the published version
    leaves the component publishing none, and the catalog then falls
    through to the highest numbered version it still serves.

delete.description:
Remove the claims row for the `sub` in the path.

Admin-only (requires `admin:delete`) and CSRF-protected. Distinct from `PUT` with empty claims. Deletion drops the row, so the user returns to the reader preset on their next request. An empty `PUT` keeps the row as an explicit revocation.

Returns `{"deleted_count": N}`. A missing row is `deleted_count: 0` (not 404), matching the unified delete-count envelope used across every admin controller. Writes an attributable audit log entry on success.
